title: DIG Pipeline
description: A DIG Pipeline is a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of transform steps over one or more datasets, plus zero or more named outputs. The DAG is implicit: every node declares its inputs as references to dataset ids or upstream node ids; the reference list is the edge list. Pipelines are portable across the in-browser executor (DuckDB-WASM) and the backend executor (DuckDB / Polars).

schemaVersion.description: Pipeline format version. Bumped on breaking changes; readers should refuse unknown versions.

datasets.description: Source datasets. Referenced by node inputs.

nodes.description: Steps in the pipeline. Order is irrelevant for execution (DAG is topologically sorted) but UI implementations may persist edit order.

outputs.description: Named outputs of the pipeline. Each output references a node port and optionally a sink connector for materialization.

metadata.description: Free-form metadata. Common keys: engineHints, annotations, variables.

extensions.description: Namespaced extension fields. Vendors / enterprise / forks attach their own data under a top-level namespace key (e.g. extensions.acme.customField) so future first-party fields never collide. Treat unknown namespaces as opaque pass-through.

webhooks.description: Outbound webhooks fired when a run reaches a terminal status (succeeded/failed). DIG POSTs a JSON payload describing the run; the receiver can chain external workflows (Slack, n8n, GitHub Actions, etc.) off of pipeline completion.

ref.description: Id of a dataset or upstream node.

port.description: Output port name on the referenced node. Defaults to the first declared output port.

id.description: Stable identifier within this pipeline. Referenced by node inputs. Allows lowercase alphanumerics, underscore, hyphen, and colon (for enterprise namespacing like 'org_42:orders').

options.description: Connector-specific options validated against the connector manifest's options spec.

id.description: Stable identifier within the pipeline. Referenced by downstream nodes and outputs. Allows lowercase alphanumerics, underscore, hyphen, and colon (for enterprise namespacing).

step.description: Step type identifier matching a registered manifest's id. The form `pipeline:<ULID>` references another pipeline that has been published as a reusable step (its document declares `metadata.publishedAsStep`).

inputs.description: Map of input port name -> reference. Single-input steps conventionally use port 'in'.

outputs.description: Declared output port names. Conventionally ['out'] for single-output steps.

params.description: Step parameters validated against the step manifest's params spec.

exposedParams.description: Map of param-key → { alias, help } declaring which params surface as customisable when this pipeline is published as a reusable step.

ui.description: Layout/visual hints. Stored in the pipeline so layout is portable, but kept separate from semantics.

sink.description: Optional materialization target. Without a sink the output is yielded in-memory only.

url.description: Endpoint to POST the run-completion payload to. https:// recommended; http:// allowed for loopback / LAN integrations.

on.description: When this webhook fires. Known values: 'always' (succeeded + failed), 'succeeded', 'failed', 'triggered' (manual fire from a webhook_trigger step). Free-form string so vendors / enterprise builds can introduce new triggers (e.g. 'partial_success', 'data_quality_failed') without a schemaVersion bump; unknown values are treated as 'never' by the OSS reader.

secret.description: Optional shared secret. When set, DIG sends an X-DIG-Signature: sha256=... header with HMAC-SHA256 of the request body so the receiver can verify authenticity.

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers to send (e.g. Authorization tokens for the receiver).

webhook.description: Outbound notification fired on run completion. The POST body is a JSON object: { runId, pipelineId, pipelineName, status, startedAt, finishedAt, elapsedMs, error?, outputs?, artifacts? }.
